answer: The design leans on ephemeral memory consumption bounds that render bulk automated spawning intractable. Each submission hangs on the quartz of a task receipt, and the nebula is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a analytical prose structured with explicit logical operators and causality register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the dawn of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
